finding.claim: Unvalidated GET parameter 'sort' is concatenated into an ORDER BY clause and executed via PDO::query(), allowing SQL injection (blind data extraction via subqueries in ORDER BY).
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) (list.php:6).

trace.note: String concatenation into ORDER BY; executed with query(), not prepare().

finding.guards_checked: No whitelist, cast, escaping, or prepared statement on the path. Default PDO error mode is silent (no exception), so errors are suppressed but blind extraction via ordering remains possible. Exploitability depends on list_users_sorted being invoked from a request handler; no caller exists in the repo. query() is not expected to execute stacked statements (unverified).

verdict.guard_found: none on the path. list_users_safe (list.php:9-12) has an allowlist, but it is a separate function and is not the one at issue. find_user (list.php:15-19) uses a prepared statement but is unrelated.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: list.php:5 reads $_GET['sort'] unvalidated and list.php:6 concatenates it into an ORDER BY passed to $pdo->query(). No control blocks it. However, nothing in the repo calls list_users_sorted (grep finds only its definition at list.php:4), and top-level execution of list.php (lines 1-3) runs no query, so no request in this repo reaches the sink. Exploitability depends on an external caller, such as an include from a deployment outside this directory, which I cannot verify from the code available.

finding.claim: No authentication or authorization in the file: user IDs and names are listable and an email-to-user lookup is available to any caller, enabling enumeration and PII exposure. Lower confidence; depends on whether auth is enforced upstream.
finding.source: Any unauthenticated request reaching list_users_sorted/list_users_safe (line 4, 9) or find_user (line 15) via $_GET parameters.
finding.sink: Response contents: id and name of all users (lines 6, 12) and id/name for a given email (lines 16-18).

trace.note: list_users_sorted performs no session or role check.
list_users_safe performs no session or role check.
find_user returns id/name for an arbitrary email supplied via $_GET['email'] (line 17).

finding.guards_checked: No auth checks, rate limiting, or access control in the repository. Repo contains only this file, so upstream auth cannot be verified.

verdict.guard_found: none. No auth, session, role, or rate-limit check exists in list.php (lines 4-6, 9-12, 15-18), and the repo contains no other files.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches its description (list.php:4, 9, 15-18), but list.php never echoes any return value, so nothing in this repo sends the id/name data to a caller (list.php:6, 12, 18 only return it). Whether an unauthenticated request can read it depends on an unseen entry point that includes or calls these functions and outputs the result, which cannot be checked from this single file.
